title: Dealflow-informed model-fit scorecard and alerting playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a quantitative scorecard that ranks emerging LLM variants for commercial readiness by combining product fit metrics, inference economics, and inbound sales/partner signals. The goal is to produce a lightweight operational feed (watchlist + alerts) that informs: model onboarding prioritization, runtime optimization experiments, and sales enablement materials.
background: PM frequently receives ad-hoc requests from Sales and Solutions about new open models mentioned in RFPs or partner PoCs. Engineering and Research run bench tests on a case-by-case basis, creating duplicated effort. We need a repeatable way to triage model candidates using the combined lens of product fit, infra cost/latency, and real-world commercial signals.
success_metrics: Reduce time from model mention in CRM -> recommended triage action from 10 business days to 48 hours
>75% of models flagged by scorecard have meaningful follow-up (bench or partner trial) within 14 days
Scorecard correlates with bench outcomes: top-3 quartile models have >=80% chance of passing our quality bar for at least one canonical workload
analysis_summary: We evaluated three sources of signal: (1) product-fit proxies (task-level evals, few-shot performance on canonical prompts), (2) infra economics (tokens/s, cost per 1M tokens after quantization profiles), (3) commercial signals (CRM mentions, Slack partner threads, repo stars/commits, model license constraints). Early experiments show that infra economics and license constraints explain a large fraction of false positives in purely quality-based rankings.
proposed_scorecard_fields: Quality: benchmark score per canonical workload (normalized)
Latency: median and 95th percentile tokens/sec on Redwood runtime profiles
Cost: relative cost multiplier vs baseline (gpt-like baseline) after quantization
Stability: hallucination rate and regression delta vs baseline
Compliance: license type, export controls risk, KMS/HSM compat
Deployability: model size, quantization friendliness, supported kernels
Commercial Signal: CRM mentions (count), partner requests, viability (license commercial use)
Operational Risk: upstream model churn frequency, upstream maintainer activity
recommended_actions: Green (Top-tier): Auto-schedule small benchmark job + infra perf sweep; notify eng/research; include in weekly model-review slot
Yellow (Investigate): Assign engineer to run targeted evals and KMS/licensing check; flag for Sales with caveats
Red (Block/Reject): Document license or technical blockers; auto-respond to CS/Sales with rationale
automation_plan: Prototype pipeline: 1) Ingest CRM keyword hits and webhook from Partner Slack -> normalize into 'mention' events. 2) Lightweight runner: spin ephemeral container to run canonical prompt suite (sampled inputs) and capture quality metrics + runtime profile on small GPU. 3) Score calculation + persist to watchlist DB. 4) Alerting rules into Slack #pm-model-watchlist and create a pre-populated Linear ticket for follow-up.
integration_points: Console: surface watchlist and scorecard per model in a new 'Market Signals' tab
CRM: small integration to tag related Opportunities and attach scorecard snapshot
Research benches: add one-click 'run full eval' action from watchlist item
Infra: hook to runtime-1.x perf jobs to reuse kernel selection profiles
tradeoffs_and_risks: Precision vs recall: aggressive alerting increases chatter for eng/research. Start conservative thresholding and iterate.
Cost: running ephemeral perf/quality jobs adds infra spend; mitigate with sampling and cheap quantized passes.
Licensing ambiguity: automated license scanning is brittle; include manual review step for borderline licenses.
Operational maintenance: watchlist requires curator role to resolve stale entries; recommend rotating responsibility across PM/SE team
milestone_timeline: Week 1 (MVP): CRM ingestion + manual intake form + scorecalc prototype (serverless)
Week 2: Lightweight perf runner + automated scoring + Slack alerting
Week 3: Console surface + one-click bench integration
Week 4: Pilot with Sales (2 AEs) and Platform SEs; collect feedback and tune thresholds
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline reliably ingests CRM mentions and creates watchlist rows for new model names
Automated score for a candidate is computed end-to-end and posted to Slack within 48 hours of ingestion
Console shows watchlist entries with links to a) perf artifacts b) license summary c) recommended action
Pilot Sales users confirm watchlist items reduced ad-hoc model discovery requests by at least 50% during pilot
